blocks.h2: When Your Faucet Needs Repair or Replacement

tiles.body: A worn cartridge, washer or seal. On a good faucet, it's a quick repair.
A loose supply line, a leaking shutoff valve or a failing drain connection.
A clogged aerator or cartridge. If every faucet is weak, it may be the pipes.
Worn parts inside the valve. Old faucets may need replacing if parts aren't made anymore.

bodies: We fix leaking, dripping and stiff kitchen faucets and install new ones, including pull-down sprayers, touchless models and filtered-water taps. In an Arlington Heights kitchen that hasn't been updated since the 1970s or 1980s, the faucet is often the first upgrade.

When we install a new faucet, we check the shutoff valves and supply lines under the sink. Old multi-turn valves often won't close fully or start dripping once they're moved. We replace them while the sink is already open, so you're not calling us back for a leak a week later.

Beyond the faucet, we handle sink drains, dishwasher connections, refrigerator and ice maker lines, disposals and gas lines for ranges. For a remodel, we move or add plumbing to fit the new layout, including island sinks.

Sink backing up? See [drain cleaning](/arlington-heights/drain-cleaning). Disposal humming? See [garbage disposal repair](/arlington-heights/garbage-disposal-installation-repair). Switching to a gas range? See [gas line installation](/arlington-heights/gas-line-installation).

img.alt: Plumbing under a double kitchen sink: white PVC drain and P-trap, braided supply lines with chrome shutoff valves, and a garbage disposal

bodies: We install sinks, faucets, toilets, showerheads, tub fillers, laundry tubs and outdoor spigots, from a single swap to a full bathroom. Every install includes the connections, new shutoffs where needed and a leak check before we leave.

Bought your own fixtures? Send us the make and model and we'll confirm they'll fit your plumbing. For toilets, see [toilet installation](/arlington-heights/toilet-installation-repair). For showers, see [shower repair](/arlington-heights/shower-repair).

blocks.h2: Faucets and Fixtures in Arlington Heights Homes
blocks.intro: With most homes built between 1940 and 1989, fixture work here often turns up older plumbing behind the faucet.

items.body: In postwar homes, weak flow at a new faucet is often caused by old galvanized pipe in the wall, not the faucet. We'll tell you if that's what we see.
Valves from the 1950s through the 1980s tend to seize or drip once they're turned. We check them on every fixture job.
Many homes have one remodeled bath and one original. We match connections between old and new plumbing so everything seals properly.

blocks.h2: Faucet and Fixture Questions From Arlington Heights Homeowners

items.q: Why is the water pressure low at only one faucet?
items.preview: Usually a clogged aerator or cartridge.
items.answer: Usually a clogged aerator or a worn cartridge. Unscrew the aerator at the tip and rinse it. If that doesn't help, the cartridge or the supply line may be the issue. If several fixtures are weak, it's likely the pipes.

items.q: Can I buy my own faucet and have you install it?
items.preview: Yes. Tell us the make and model and we'll confirm it fits.
items.answer: Yes. Tell us the make and model when you call, and we'll make sure it fits your sink and plumbing before the visit.

items.q: Should I repair or replace my faucet?
items.preview: A worn part on a good faucet is a repair. A corroded or failing faucet is a replacement.
items.answer: If it's a quality faucet with a worn cartridge or seal, repair it. If the body is corroded, the finish is failing or parts aren't available, replacing it is the better value.

items.q: Can you replace several faucets in one visit?
items.preview: Yes, and it often saves a second trip.
items.answer: Yes. If several faucets are the same age and starting to drip, replacing them together saves time. You'll get one flat price for the whole job.

items.q: How much does faucet installation cost in Arlington Heights?
items.preview: It depends on the faucet and what's under the sink. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the faucet, the condition of the valves and supply lines and access. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
